name: to-spec
description: Turn the current conversation into a spec and publish it to the project issue tracker — no interview, just synthesis of what you've already discussed.
disable-model-invocation: true
---

This skill takes the current conversation context and codebase understanding and produces a spec (you may know this document as a PRD). Do NOT interview the user — just synthesize what you already know.

The issue tracker and triage label vocabulary should have been provided to you — run `/setup-matt-pocock-skills` if not.

## Process

1. Explore the repo to understand the current state of the codebase, if you haven't already. Use the project's domain glossary vocabulary throughout the spec, and respect any ADRs in the area you're touching.

2. Sketch out the seams at which you're going to test the feature. Existing seams should be preferred to new ones. Use the highest seam possible. If new seams are needed, propose them at the highest point you can. The fewer seams across the codebase, the better - the ideal number is one.

Check with the user that these seams match their expectations.

3. Write the spec using the template below, then publish it to the project issue tracker. Apply the `ready-for-agent` triage label - no need for additional triage.

<spec-template>

## Problem Statement

The problem that the user is facing, from the user's perspective.

## Solution

The solution to the problem, from the user's perspective.

## User Stories

A LONG, numbered list of user stories. Each user story should be in the format of:

1. As an <actor>, I want a <feature>, so that <benefit>

<user-story-example>
1. As a mobile bank customer, I want to see balance on my accounts, so that I can make better informed decisions about my spending
</user-story-example>

This list of user stories should be extremely extensive and cover all aspects of the feature.

## Implementation Decisions

A list of implementation decisions that were made. This can include:

- The modules that will be built/modified
- The interfaces of those modules that will be modified
- Technical clarifications from the developer
- Architectural decisions
- Schema changes
- API contracts
- Specific interactions

Do NOT include specific file paths or code snippets. They may end up being outdated very quickly.

Exception: if a prototype produced a snippet that encodes a decision more precisely than prose can (state machine, reducer, schema, type shape), inline it within the relevant decision and note briefly that it came from a prototype. Trim to the decision-rich parts — not a working demo, just the important bits.

## Testing Decisions

A list of testing decisions that were made. Include:

- A description of what makes a good test (only test external behavior, not implementation details)
- Which modules will be tested
- Prior art for the tests (i.e. similar types of tests in the codebase)

## Out of Scope

A description of the things that are out of scope for this spec.

## Further Notes

Any further notes about the feature.

</spec-template>

</skill>

I’m using the `to-spec` skill to synthesize issue #1 against the repository’s domain language and architecture. I’ll inspect the issue, relevant plans/decisions, and existing test seams first; the skill requires a quick seam check with you before I publish the finished spec.

Issue #1 is a completed planning map, and its linked decisions already define the MVP in detail. I’m treating those resolved child tickets—not the superseded multi-user PRD/feature plans—as the source of truth, then checking the current code only to identify the cleanest behavioral test boundary.

Proposed test seams before I publish the spec:

- Primary: route-level user behavior through React Testing Library for Capture, completion, correction, Recent Sightings, and Plan.
- Persistence: the explicit sighting operations against disposable real PostgreSQL.
- Operations: black-box migration/startup and health-endpoint behavior.
- Final acceptance: the resolved physical iPhone Safari journey.

These match issue #8 and keep testing at the highest practical boundaries. Do these seams match your expectations?
Yeah sure

The seams are confirmed. I’m now publishing the synthesized implementation spec as a new GitHub issue with only the `ready-for-agent` triage label; the spec will preserve #1’s resolved scope, algorithms, operational contract, and acceptance boundaries.

## Problem Statement

The current application scaffolding represents a superseded crowdsourced, multi-user, location-aware product. It requires authentication, store identity, moderation, synchronization, and other infrastructure before its essential value exists.

The user needs a private, mobile-first tool that works in the moment while approaching a warming shelf: quickly record the date and time printed on a rotisserie chicken label, optionally record doneness, correct mistakes, and use accumulated sightings to choose a historically promising weekday and approximate time. The application must preserve the label facts exactly as printed, remain understandable when history is sparse, and run reliably as a self-hosted application against an operator-provided PostgreSQL database.

## Solution

Rebuild the application around one private chicken-tracking core loop with no application-level identity or location model.

Capture is the default mobile destination. A new sighting starts with the device's current local date and minute, allows correction, and is durably saved before optional doneness enrichment. An unmistakable full-screen completion state lets the user add light, medium, or dark doneness, correct the saved sighting, or finish. Capture also shows the three most recently created sightings for correction or confirmed deletion.

Plan is the second and only other top-level destination. It evaluates a selected weekday and approximate time against distinct historical label dates within an inclusive rolling ±10-minute window. It reports a non-probabilistic planner signal—One of the better times, About typical, or One of the quieter times—together with its supporting distinct-date count and explicit empty or sparse-history states.

Persist only the timezone-free label date and clock minute, optional doneness, and audit instants in a fresh PostgreSQL schema. Ship the application as one stateless OCI container that migrates before startup, exposes database-aware health, and delegates TLS, private access, PostgreSQL provisioning, backups, and restores to the operator.

## User Stories

1. As the tracker, I want Capture to be the default destination, so that I can record a sighting immediately.
2. As the tracker approaching the warming shelf, I want a new sighting to default to my device's current local date and minute, so that the common capture requires minimal input.
3. As the tracker, I want label time to be the most prominent editable field, so that I can quickly verify the most important fact.
4. As the tracker, I want the current label date visible without dominating the capture surface, so that I can verify it at a glance.
5. As the tracker, I want to expand the date control when correction is necessary, so that full date editing remains available without slowing normal capture.
6. As the tracker, I want to edit both label date and label time before saving, so that an inaccurate default never has to be accepted.
7. As the tracker, I want label time stored exactly as printed without timezone conversion, so that travel, server settings, and daylight-saving changes cannot alter it.
8. As the tracker, I want any complete real calendar date accepted, so that I can backfill older sightings.
9. As the tracker, I want any valid clock minute accepted, so that the recorded sighting faithfully reflects the label.
10. As the tracker, I want a non-blocking warning for label times before 9:00 AM or after 8:00 PM, so that likely mistakes are visible without preventing valid data entry.
11. As the tracker, I want one clear Save label time action, so that capture can finish quickly while I am moving.
12. As the tracker, I want saving to durably create the sighting before optional enrichment begins, so that the essential label facts cannot be lost if I stop or reload.
13. As the tracker, I want pending feedback while a sighting is saving, so that I do not submit it repeatedly.
14. As the tracker, I want failed saves to preserve my entered label facts, so that I can retry without re-entering them.
15. As the tracker, I want a failed initial save never to look successful, so that I can trust the application's confirmation.
16. As the tracker, I want a full-screen completion state after a durable save, so that success is unmistakable.
17. As the tracker, I want to select light, medium, or dark doneness after saving label time, so that the optional assessment never blocks the essential sighting.
18. As the tracker, I want to finish without choosing doneness, so that doneness remains genuinely optional.
19. As the tracker, I want a doneness choice to update the saved sighting immediately, so that my assessment is durable before I leave the completion screen.
20. As the tracker, I want the completion screen to remain until I tap Done, so that an immediate update does not produce a surprising navigation change.
21. As the tracker, I want an enrichment failure to leave the original sighting stored and correctable, so that optional data cannot undo a successful save.
22. As the tracker, I want Done to return me to a fresh Capture screen, so that the application is ready for another sighting.
23. As the tracker, I want the newly saved sighting first in Recent Sightings, so that I can verify it immediately.
24. As the tracker, I want to correct the saved sighting directly from completion, so that mistakes discovered immediately are easy to fix.
25. As the tracker, I want to see the three most recently created sightings on Capture, so that likely corrections are close at hand.
26. As the tracker, I want Recent Sightings ordered by durable creation rather than edited label time, so that correction does not unexpectedly reorder the list.
27. As the tracker, I want to open the same full-screen correction flow from any recent sighting, so that correction behavior is consistent.
28. As the tracker, I want correction to replace the full label date, label minute, and optional doneness together, so that the saved record has one coherent state.
29. As the tracker, I want Cancel to leave a sighting unchanged, so that merely opening or editing the form does not mutate it.
30. As the tracker, I want correction failures to leave the persisted and visible sighting intact, so that errors do not create false state.
31. As the tracker, I want deletion protected by explicit confirmation, so that an accidental tap cannot permanently remove a sighting.
32. As the tracker, I want a confirmed deletion to permanently remove the sighting, so that incorrect records no longer influence history.
33. As the tracker, I want deletion failures to leave the sighting visible and stored, so that the UI does not claim an unsuccessful change.
34. As the tracker, I want a stable not-found state when a sighting no longer exists, so that stale correction links fail clearly.
35. As the tracker, I want Capture and Plan as the only persistent bottom-navigation destinations, so that the mobile application remains focused.
36. As the tracker, I want bottom navigation hidden during completion and correction, so that focused flows are not interrupted.
37. As the tracker, I want Plan to default to my device's current local weekday and time, so that it answers the question most likely to matter now.
38. As the tracker, I want to phrase my plan as “I'm going [weekday] around [time],” so that the controls match the decision I am making.
39. As the tracker, I want the planner to recalculate immediately after changing weekday or time, so that no separate Submit action is needed.
40. As the tracker, I want planner evidence limited to label dates on the selected literal weekday, so that timezone conversion cannot change historical grouping.
41. As the tracker, I want the selected time compared with sightings from 10 minutes before through 10 minutes after it, so that the result reflects a useful visit window.
42. As the tracker, I want sightings exactly 10 minutes before or after the selected time included, so that the window boundary is predictable.
43. As the tracker, I want planner windows to stop at weekday boundaries rather than wrap across midnight, so that evidence remains attached to the selected weekday.
44. As the tracker, I want multiple matching sightings on one historical date counted once, so that repeated same-day observations do not overstate evidence.
45. As the tracker, I want every planner result to show its supporting distinct-date count, so that I can judge the amount of evidence.
46. As the tracker, I want the planner to distinguish One of the better times, About typical, and One of the quieter times, so that historical comparisons are easy to understand.
47. As the tracker, I want planner language to avoid probabilities and forecasts, so that historical evidence is not presented as a calibrated prediction.
48. As the tracker, I want No history for this weekday when none exists, so that absent evidence is not confused with a poor time.
49. As the tracker, I want No matching sightings yet when the weekday has history but the selected window has no matches, so that a zero-match window is explicit.
50. As the tracker, I want Not enough history to compare yet when evidence is too sparse for relative ranking, so that weak data is not overstated.
51. As the tracker, I want sparse and empty states to explain that plans improve as I record sightings, so that I understand how to make the planner more useful.
52. As the tracker, I want a Record a sighting action from Plan's empty and sparse states, so that I can immediately contribute useful history.
53. As the tracker, I want duplicate label dates and times accepted, so that real observations are not rejected as conflicts.
54. As the tracker, I want the interface to use a consistent 12-hour clock with AM/PM and unambiguous detailed dates, so that label facts are easy to read.
55. As the tracker using a phone, I want semantic controls, visible focus, clear status announcements, and adequate touch targets, so that the core loop remains accessible and mistake-resistant.
56. As the tracker on a narrow screen, I want Capture, correction, and Plan to avoid horizontal overflow, so that all essential actions remain usable.
57. As the operator, I want the application to require only a PostgreSQL connection secret, so that deployment configuration stays small.
58. As the operator, I want schema migrations to run before the web server starts, so that the application never serves against an incompatible schema.
59. As the operator, I want migration failure to stop startup, so that a broken deployment fails visibly.
60. As the operator, I want a standalone migration command, so that I can recover or diagnose migration problems.
61. As the operator, I want a health endpoint that checks both the web process and PostgreSQL connectivity, so that monitoring reflects actual readiness.
62. As the operator, I want immutable public container versions, so that deployments and rollbacks are reproducible.
63. As the operator, I want the previous compatible container version to remain deployable, so that application rollback does not require an emergency database rollback.
64. As the operator, I want the application container to own no persistent volume or gateway state, so that recovery consists of redeploying an image against reachable PostgreSQL.
65. As the operator, I want the external gateway to own TLS and private access control, so that the application does not duplicate network security responsibilities.
66. As the operator, I want clear backup and restore expectations, so that sighting history can be recovered after database loss.
67. As the implementer, I want each delivery checkpoint to end in a runnable, reviewable, green state, so that the rebuild can progress safely.
68. As the implementer, I want unfinished destinations hidden rather than represented by placeholders, so that intermediate releases remain coherent.
69. As the implementer, I want current product documentation to describe only the private core loop, so that superseded crowdsourcing requirements do not guide new code.
70. As the implementer, I want a versioned acceptance record for the completed MVP, so that handoff evidence is reproducible.

## Implementation Decisions

- The resolved Wayfinder map and its child decisions are the source of truth. The previous multi-user, crowdsourced, location-aware PRD and feature plans are superseded.
- Retain the TanStack Start/Vite application foundation, TypeScript, generic Shadcn UI primitives and design tokens, PostgreSQL/Drizzle tooling, and the Vitest/React Testing Library harness.
- Remove application authentication, users, invitations, sessions, roles, profiles, trust scoring, moderation, approvals, rate limits, admin surfaces, and their supporting dependencies and configuration.
- Remove stores, store selection, GPS and proximity behavior, store synchronization, and cross-store aggregation. Location remains only a possible future capability.
- Use exactly two top-level mobile destinations: Capture and Plan. Capture is the default route. The Visit planner has its own route, and correction uses an identity-addressed full-screen route. Reserve a secondary Plan route for future historical exploration, but do not implement or expose it in this MVP.
- Show persistent bottom navigation only when both Capture and Plan are functional. Hide it during save completion and correction.
- Use the Save-then-enrich interaction. Initialize capture from the client's current local date and minute, make label time prominent, keep date compact but fully editable, and durably create before displaying completion.
- Accept complete real dates and all clock minutes. Show an Outside store hours warning before 9:00 AM or after 8:00 PM without blocking save.
- Completion is full-screen and begins only after successful durable creation. Doneness is optional and constrained to light, medium, or dark. Selecting or clearing doneness uses a targeted update; Done is a separate action.
- After Done, return to fresh Capture with the saved sighting first in Recent Sightings. Correction from completion and correction from Recent Sightings use the same editor.
- Show exactly the three most recently created sightings on Capture. Order deterministically by creation instant descending and identity descending. Label-time correction does not change recency.
- Correction fully replaces label date, label minute, and nullable doneness. Deletion is a confirmed hard delete. Do not add generic patching, optimistic locking, soft deletion, or recovery.
- Return to the originating screen after Save, Cancel, or successful confirmed deletion from correction.
- Represent label time as a literal, timezone-free calendar date plus minute after midnight. Do not store it as a timestamp, convert it to UTC, attach an offset, or store seconds or formatted display text.
- Derive historical weekdays directly from the stored label date. Format user-facing time with a 12-hour clock and AM/PM, and use an unambiguous written date in detailed contexts.
- Replace the existing schema and generated migrations with a fresh baseline. Preserve no existing data and provide no compatibility path.
- Use one sightings table. It has a server-generated integer identity; required label date; required small integer label minute constrained from 0 through 1439; nullable text doneness constrained to light, medium, or dark; immutable creation instant; and application-maintained update instant.
- Duplicate label dates and times are valid. The schema has no user, location, timezone, soft-delete, or concurrency-version columns.
- Add only the primary-key index and a descending creation-instant/identity index for Recent Sightings. Add planner-specific indexes only after profiling demonstrates a need.
- Expose explicit create, full correction, targeted doneness, and hard-delete mutations. Each successful mutation returns the complete resulting sighting except deletion, which returns the deleted identity. Missing identities return structured not-found results.
- Expose identity lookup, deterministic recent listing, and distinct weekday evidence reads. Add no general-purpose search/list contract. The deferred historical grid will receive a purpose-built query when implemented.
- Initially calculate the planner signal in application logic. Moving it into PostgreSQL is allowed only when profiling justifies the change and observable behavior remains unchanged.
- Build weekday evidence from distinct label-date/label-minute pairs whose literal label date falls on the selected weekday.
- Score a window by the number of distinct historical dates with at least one label minute inclusively within 10 minutes of its center. Do not wrap across midnight.
- Build the comparison population from one candidate centered on every distinct observed label minute for the selected weekday. Duplicate minutes do not create candidates; overlapping windows remain distinct candidates.
- Evaluate planner states in this order: no weekday history; zero selected-window matches; insufficient comparison evidence; comparative band.
- Comparative bands require at least four distinct historical dates and at least three distinct candidate minutes. Otherwise return Not enough history to compare yet.
- For an eligible population of size N, count candidate scores strictly lower and strictly higher than the selected score. Return One of the better times when three times the lower count is at least two times N. Otherwise return One of the quieter times when three times the higher count is at least two times N. Otherwise return About typical.
- Equal scores count neither above nor below, moving tied evidence toward About typical. Use integer comparisons without percentile interpolation or floating-point boundaries.
- Every planner state exposes the selected window's distinct-date count. Empty and sparse states provide coaching and a direct action back to Capture. Database failures are presented distinctly from valid empty history.
- Implement in eight independently reviewable checkpoints: current documentation; clean foundation and persistence; durable Capture; completion and doneness; correction/deletion/recent; Visit planner; deployment and operations; final acceptance and reconciliation.
- Each checkpoint is a vertical slice containing server behavior, UI, failures, tests, and affected documentation. Every checkpoint must pass lint, typecheck, applicable tests, and production build.
- Distribute one stateless OCI application container through GitHub Container Registry with a convenience latest tag and immutable version tags. Production deployments should pin a version and retain the previous known-good version.
- PostgreSQL is operator-provided through required DATABASE_URL configuration. The application container does not provision PostgreSQL or own persistent storage.
- Apply committed forward-only Drizzle migrations before server startup. Migration failure prevents serving. Retain a standalone migration command.
- Migrations remain compatible with the immediately preceding application release to support container rollback without database rollback.
- Serve plain HTTP on an internal port. An external private gateway owns TLS, routing, access control, and prevention of untrusted public exposure.
- Expose a health endpoint that verifies both web-process and database availability.
- Delegate PostgreSQL provisioning, backups, and restores to the operator. Document automated daily backups, at least seven days of retention, and a tested restore path.
- Reconcile active product and implementation documentation with this private core-loop spec throughout delivery. Preserve superseded rationale only as historical context.

## Testing Decisions

- Tests assert externally observable behavior rather than internal component state, implementation structure, SQL construction, or private helper calls.
- The primary product seam is route-level behavior rendered through React Testing Library. Exercise Capture, completion, correction, Recent Sightings, Plan, navigation visibility, accessible status, empty states, failure states, and controlled-clock behavior through what a user can see and do.
- The persistence seam is the explicit sighting mutation and read contract against a disposable real PostgreSQL instance. Database mocks may support narrow unit tests but do not count as acceptance evidence.
- The operations seam is black-box migration/startup and health behavior: successful migrate-then-start, refusal after migration failure, refusal without DATABASE_URL, healthy status with PostgreSQL available, and unhealthy status after connectivity loss.
- The assembled-experience seam is a concise manual mobile journey. A mandatory full browser-automation suite is not required for this MVP; add one later only if observed regressions reveal a material gap.
- Existing pure-function Vitest tests demonstrate deterministic fixture style, and existing database-oriented tests demonstrate dependency isolation, but superseded auth and store-sync tests are removed with their obsolete modules.
- Use a controlled client clock to verify current defaults, minute and calendar transitions, literal weekday behavior, outside-store-hours warnings, and deterministic 12-hour/date formatting.
- Verify the Save-then-enrich ordering explicitly. A failed initial save preserves entered facts and never displays completion. A successful create followed by failed enrichment leaves the sighting durably stored and correctable.
- Verify correction Save and Cancel, confirmed deletion, stable not-found behavior, and failures that leave persisted and visible state unchanged.
- Verify Recent Sightings returns only the top three in creation-instant/identity order, including tied creation instants, backfills, and edits that do not reorder recency.
- Verify PostgreSQL schema constraints and every explicit create, correction, enrichment, deletion, identity lookup, recent-list, and weekday-evidence contract against the fresh migration.
- Planner fixtures cover literal weekdays, inclusive ±10-minute boundaries, no midnight wrapping, distinct-date deduplication, duplicate candidate-minute removal, overlapping candidates, deterministic input-order independence, every state-precedence branch, both evidence gates, all three bands, fully tied populations, zero-match, and no-weekday-history states.
- The comparative classifier includes the resolved boundary fixtures: scores [1,2,3] classify selected 3/2/1 as better/typical/quieter; [2,2,3] classify 3 as better and 2 as typical; [1,2,2] classifies 1 as quieter; [2,2,2] classifies 2 as typical; and [1,2,3,4] classifies 3 as typical and 4 as better. Mirrored quieter cases also apply.
- Planner/database failures must remain distinguishable from valid no-history, zero-match, and insufficient-comparison states.
- Accessibility coverage verifies semantic controls, visible labels, logical headings, keyboard operation, visible focus, announced validation/status changes, adequate touch targets, and token-based contrast. Use automated accessibility checks where practical and manual keyboard/focus checks.
- Required automated gates are lint, typecheck, all Vitest suites, production build, and real-PostgreSQL integration tests, with no accepted flaky or known-failing exceptions. No arbitrary line-coverage threshold is required.
- Run a roughly ten-minute manual acceptance journey against an isolated, resettable, deterministically seeded database on a physical iPhone 15 Pro with current Safari.
- The manual journey covers portrait behavior from 375 through 430 CSS pixels, capture, reload after durable save before enrichment, doneness, correction, cancel, confirmed deletion, recency, planner adjustment, empty states, focus/keyboard behavior, narrow-screen overflow, and an injected enrichment failure.
- Support current stable Chrome and the immediately previous major version. Landscape optimization, tablets, legacy browsers, desktop-specific polish, formal WCAG certification, and exhaustive screen-reader testing are not acceptance requirements.
- Keep a concise versioned Markdown acceptance record containing the tested commit and date, commands and results, PostgreSQL version, physical device and browser, responsive viewport checks, journey result, and accepted limitations.

## Out of Scope

- Multiple users, authentication, invitations, sessions, roles, profiles, trust scoring, moderation, approvals, rate limits, and administration.
- Store or location identity, store selection, GPS, proximity checks, store synchronization, and aggregate cross-store views.
- Migration or preservation of existing application data.
- Notes or free-text sighting fields; doneness is the only optional sighting attribute.
- Predictive probabilities, forecasts, commute windows, notifications, native mobile applications, and offline-first behavior.
- Application-managed PostgreSQL provisioning, backup infrastructure, TLS, routing, or private-network access.
- The switchable 15-minute historical frequency/doneness grid, its selected-bucket summary, planner-to-history cross-link, and a visible history route or placeholder.
- General sighting search, a complete history list, planner-specific database optimization without measured need, soft deletion, recovery, and optimistic locking.
- Mandatory end-to-end browser automation, numeric test-coverage targets, landscape-specific optimization, tablet support, legacy-browser support, desktop-specific polish, formal accessibility certification, and exhaustive screen-reader testing.

## Further Notes

- This spec synthesizes the completed planning map in #1 and the resolved decisions linked from that map.
- Canonical language is: sighting, label time, doneness, Visit plan, and planner signal. Avoid submission, report, purchase, observation time, batch time, rating, quality score, prediction, forecast, probability, and likelihood score.
- The richer historical view remains a planned follow-up: one switchable weekday-by-time grid with fixed 15-minute cells, sightings frequency by default, doneness on demand, selected-cell preservation, observed counts for sparse frequency cells, and insufficient-data treatment for doneness cells with fewer than four sightings.
- The current repository is intentionally expected to change substantially. Its authentication, user, store, synchronization, and multi-user schema code reflects superseded scope rather than migration constraints.

2. As the tracker, I want a new sighting to default to my device's current local date and minute, so that normal capture needs minimal input.
3. As the tracker, I want label time to be the prominent editable field, so that I can verify the essential fact quickly.
4. As the tracker, I want the date visible in a compact control with full correction available, so that normal capture stays fast without blocking backfills.
5. As the tracker, I want to edit label date and time before saving, so that an inaccurate default is never forced.
6. As the tracker, I want label time preserved without timezone conversion, so that server settings, travel, and daylight-saving changes cannot alter it.
7. As the tracker, I want any complete real date and valid clock minute accepted, so that I can record exactly what the label says.
8. As the tracker, I want a non-blocking Outside store hours warning before 9:00 AM or after 8:00 PM, so that likely mistakes are visible without rejecting valid data.
9. As the tracker, I want one clear Save label time action, so that I can finish capture while moving.
10. As the tracker, I want Save to durably create the sighting before optional enrichment, so that the essential facts survive interruption or reload.
11. As the tracker, I want pending feedback and duplicate-submit protection, so that I know saving is underway.
12. As the tracker, I want a failed initial save to preserve my input and never show success, so that I can retry confidently.
13. As the tracker, I want unmistakable full-screen completion after durable save, so that I know the sighting exists.
14. As the tracker, I want to select light, medium, or dark doneness after saving, so that optional assessment never blocks the sighting.
15. As the tracker, I want to finish without choosing doneness, so that doneness remains optional.
16. As the tracker, I want doneness updates to be durable while completion remains open until Done, so that persistence and navigation are predictable.
17. As the tracker, I want enrichment failure to preserve the created sighting, so that optional data cannot undo a successful save.
18. As the tracker, I want Done to return to fresh Capture with the new sighting first in Recent Sightings, so that I can verify it and capture again.
19. As the tracker, I want to correct a sighting directly from completion, so that immediate mistakes are easy to fix.
20. As the tracker, I want to see the three most recently created sightings, so that likely corrections stay close at hand.
21. As the tracker, I want Recent Sightings ordered by creation rather than label time, so that backfills and edits do not reorder it unexpectedly.
22. As the tracker, I want one consistent full-screen correction flow, so that correction behaves the same from completion and Recent Sightings.
23. As the tracker, I want correction to replace label date, label minute, and nullable doneness together, so that each sighting remains coherent.
24. As the tracker, I want Cancel and failed correction to leave the sighting unchanged, so that unsaved edits never leak into persisted state.
25. As the tracker, I want deletion behind explicit confirmation, so that an accidental tap cannot permanently remove a sighting.
26. As the tracker, I want successful deletion to remove the sighting and failed deletion to leave it visible, so that UI and persistence agree.
27. As the tracker, I want a stable not-found state for a missing sighting, so that stale correction links fail clearly.
28. As the tracker, I want Capture and Plan as the only bottom-navigation destinations, so that the app stays focused.
29. As the tracker, I want bottom navigation hidden during completion and correction, so that focused flows are not interrupted.
30. As the tracker, I want Plan to default to the device's current local weekday and time, so that it answers my most likely question.
31. As the tracker, I want to adjust “I'm going [weekday] around [time]” and see immediate recalculation, so that planning needs no Submit action.
32. As the tracker, I want evidence limited to the selected literal weekday, so that timezone conversion cannot change historical grouping.
33. As the tracker, I want exact matches from 10 minutes before through 10 minutes after included, so that the visit window is useful and predictable.
34. As the tracker, I want windows not to wrap across midnight, so that evidence remains attached to the selected weekday.
35. As the tracker, I want multiple matches from one historical date counted once, so that repeated observations do not overstate evidence.
36. As the tracker, I want every planner state to show its distinct-date count, so that I can judge the evidence.
37. As the tracker, I want better, typical, and quieter bands rather than probabilities, so that history is not presented as a forecast.
38. As the tracker, I want No history for this weekday when none exists, so that absent evidence is not confused with a poor time.
39. As the tracker, I want No matching sightings yet when weekday history exists but my window has none, so that zero matches are explicit.
40. As the tracker, I want Not enough history to compare yet when evidence is sparse, so that weak data is not overstated.
41. As the tracker, I want sparse states to explain that the plan improves with more sightings and link to Capture, so that I can act on them.
42. As the tracker, I want duplicate label dates and times accepted, so that legitimate observations are not rejected.
43. As the tracker, I want consistent 12-hour times and unambiguous detailed dates, so that sightings are easy to read.
44. As the tracker using a phone or keyboard, I want semantic controls, visible focus, announced statuses, adequate targets, and no narrow-screen overflow, so that the core loop remains accessible.
45. As the operator, I want DATABASE_URL to be the only required secret, so that configuration stays small.
46. As the operator, I want migrations to complete before serving and failures to stop startup, so that incompatible schema is never served.
47. As the operator, I want a standalone migration command and database-aware health endpoint, so that recovery and monitoring are practical.
48. As the operator, I want immutable container versions and compatibility with the preceding release, so that rollback is reproducible.
49. As the operator, I want the stateless app to delegate TLS, access, PostgreSQL lifecycle, backups, and restores, so that responsibilities are clear.
50. As the implementer, I want every checkpoint runnable, reviewable, documented, and green without dead placeholders, so that the rebuild can progress safely.
51. As the implementer, I want a versioned acceptance record, so that the completed MVP has reproducible handoff evidence.

## Implementation Decisions

- The completed Wayfinder map and resolved child tickets are the source of truth. The old
  multi-user/location PRD and feature plans are superseded.
- Retain TanStack Start/Vite, strict TypeScript, generic Shadcn primitives/design tokens,
  PostgreSQL/Drizzle tooling, and Vitest/React Testing Library.
- Remove authentication, users, invitations, sessions, roles, profiles, trust, moderation,
  approvals, rate limits, admin, stores, GPS/proximity, store synchronization, cross-store
  aggregation, and supporting dependencies and configuration.
- Use exactly Capture and Plan as top-level destinations. Capture is default; correction is an
  identity-addressed full-screen route. Reserve a secondary Plan route for future history but
  do not implement or expose it in the MVP.
- Use Save-then-enrich. Defaults come from the client clock. Durable create precedes
  completion; optional doneness uses a targeted update; Done separately returns to Capture.
- Show exactly three Recent Sightings ordered by creation instant descending, then identity
  descending. Editing label facts does not change recency.
- Correction fully replaces label date, label minute, and nullable doneness. Deletion is a
  confirmed hard delete. Do not add generic patch, optimistic locking, soft delete, or recovery.
- Label time is a literal timezone-free date and minute after midnight. Store no timestamp,
  timezone, offset, seconds, or formatted time. Derive weekday directly from label date.
- Replace the existing schema and generated migrations with a fresh baseline and no data or
  compatibility path.
- Use one sightings table with server-generated integer identity; required date; required
  small integer minute constrained to 0–1439; nullable text doneness constrained to light,
  medium, or dark; immutable creation instant; and application-maintained update instant.
  Duplicate label facts are valid.
- Add only the primary key and a descending creation/identity Recent Sightings index initially.
- Expose explicit create, full correction, targeted doneness, and hard-delete mutations;
  identity lookup, deterministic recent listing, and distinct weekday evidence reads; and
  structured not-found results. Add no general search contract.
- Initially calculate the planner signal in application logic. Move it to PostgreSQL and add
  specialized indexing only after profiling, without changing observable behavior.
- Build evidence from distinct label-date/minute pairs for the selected literal weekday. Score
  a center by distinct dates with at least one minute inclusively within ±10 minutes, without
  midnight wrapping.
- Build one comparison candidate per distinct observed minute. Duplicate minutes do not create
  candidates; overlapping candidates remain separate.
- Resolve states in order: no weekday history; zero selected-window matches; insufficient
  comparison; comparative band. Comparative bands require at least four historical dates and
  three candidate minutes.
- For population size N, return better when 3 × strictly-lower scores ≥ 2 × N; otherwise quieter
  when 3 × strictly-higher scores ≥ 2 × N; otherwise typical. Ties count neither way.
- Keep database failures distinct from valid empty states. Every state shows selected-window
  evidence; empty/sparse states coach and link to Capture.
- Deliver eight green vertical checkpoints: current docs; clean foundation/persistence;
  durable Capture; completion/doneness; correction/deletion/recent; Visit planner;
  deployment/operations; final acceptance/reconciliation.
- Ship one stateless public GHCR image with latest and immutable version tags. Production pins
  a version and retains the previous known-good version.
- Use operator-provided PostgreSQL through required DATABASE_URL. Apply forward-only committed
  migrations before startup; stop on failure; retain standalone migration. Keep migrations
  compatible with the immediately preceding app release.
- Serve plain HTTP internally. The external gateway owns TLS, routing, and private access.
  Health verifies the web process and PostgreSQL. The operator owns provisioning, daily
  backups with at least seven days retention, and a tested restore path.
- Update affected documentation in each checkpoint, using canonical domain language and
  preserving superseded rationale only as history.

## Testing Decisions

- Test external behavior, not component state, SQL construction, or private helpers.
- The primary product seam is route-level behavior through React Testing Library: Capture,
  completion, correction, Recent Sightings, Plan, navigation, accessibility, empty/error
  states, and controlled-clock behavior.
- The persistence seam is the public sighting operation/read contract against disposable real
  PostgreSQL. Mocks may support unit tests but are not acceptance evidence.
- The operations seam is black-box migrate/start/health behavior.
- The assembled seam is a concise manual mobile journey. Mandatory browser E2E is not required
  unless later regressions reveal a gap.
- Existing pure-function tests are prior art for deterministic fixtures; existing
  database-oriented tests show dependency isolation. Remove obsolete auth/store tests with
  their modules.
- Verify clock/calendar transitions, literal weekdays, warnings, formatting, durable
  Save-then-enrich failure ordering, correction/cancel/delete/not-found behavior, deterministic
  top-three recency, constraints, and every explicit persistence operation.
- Planner fixtures cover inclusive boundaries, no midnight wrapping, date deduplication,
  duplicate candidate removal, overlaps, input-order independence, state precedence, both
  evidence gates, all bands, ties, zero match, and no weekday history.
- Required band fixtures include: [1,2,3] with selected 3/2/1 => better/typical/quieter;
  [2,2,3] with 3 => better and 2 => typical; [1,2,2] with 1 => quieter; [2,2,2] with 2 =>

- Verify semantic controls, labels, headings, keyboard use, focus, announced statuses, target

- Required automated gates are lint, typecheck, all Vitest suites, production build, and

- Run a roughly ten-minute journey on physical iPhone 15 Pro/current Safari against isolated,

## Out of Scope

- Multiple users, application auth, invitations, roles, profiles, trust, moderation, approvals,
  rate limits, and administration.
- Location/store identity, selection, GPS, proximity, synchronization, and cross-store views.
- Existing-data migration; notes/free text; probabilities, forecasts, commute windows,

- App-managed PostgreSQL, backups, TLS, routing, or access.
- The 15-minute switchable historical frequency/doneness grid, planner cross-link, and any

- General search/history lists, speculative planner indexing, soft deletion, recovery,
  optimistic locking, mandatory browser E2E, coverage targets, landscape/tablet/legacy-browser
  polish, formal WCAG certification, and exhaustive screen-reader testing.

# Ask Matt

You don't remember every skill, so ask.

A **flow** is a path through the skills. Most paths run along one **main flow**, and two **on-ramps** merge onto it. Everything else is standalone, or a vocabulary layer that runs underneath.

## The main flow: idea → ship

The route most work travels. You have an idea and want it built.

1. **`/grill-with-docs`** — sharpen the idea by interview. Start here when you **have a codebase**: it's stateful, retaining what it learns in `CONTEXT.md` and ADRs. (No codebase? Use `/grill-me` — see Standalone. Both run the same `/grilling` primitive; `grill-with-docs` is the one that leaves a paper trail.)
2. **Branch — can you settle every question in conversation?** If a question needs a runnable answer (state, business logic, a UI you have to see), detour through a prototype, bridged by **`/handoff`** in both directions (see Crossing sessions):
   - **`/handoff`** out, then open a fresh session against that file,
   - **`/prototype`** to answer the question with throwaway code,
   - **`/handoff`** back what you learned, and reference it from the original idea thread.
3. **Branch — is this a multi-session build?**
   - **Yes** → **`/to-spec`** (turn the thread into a spec), then **`/to-tickets`** to split it into tracer-bullet tickets, each declaring its **blocking edges**. On a local tracker that's one file per ticket under `.scratch/<feature>/issues/`, worked blockers-first by hand; on a real tracker the edges become native blocking links, so any ticket whose blockers are done can be grabbed — kick off **`/implement`** per ticket, **clearing context between each one**.
   - **No** → **`/implement`** right here, in the same context window.

   Either way, **`/implement`** builds each issue by driving **`/tdd`** internally — one red-green slice at a time — then closes out by running **`/code-review`**, a two-axis review (Standards + Spec) of the diff, before committing. Reach for **`/tdd`** on its own when you just want to build a concrete behaviour test-first without a full spec, and **`/code-review`** on its own whenever you want to review a branch or PR against a fixed point.

### Context hygiene

Keep steps 1–3 in **one unbroken context window** — don't compact or clear until after `/to-tickets` — so the grilling, spec, and tickets all build on the same thinking. Each `/implement` then starts fresh, working from the ticket.

The limit on this is the **[smart zone](https://www.aihero.dev/ai-coding-dictionary/smart-zone)**: the window (~120k tokens on state-of-the-art models) within which the model still reasons sharply. If a session approaches it before `/to-tickets`, don't push on degraded — `/handoff` and continue in a fresh thread.

## On-ramps

A starting situation that generates work, then merges onto the main flow.

- **Bugs and requests piling up** → **`/triage`**. It moves issues through triage roles and produces agent-ready issues, which **`/implement`** later picks up.

  Triage is only for issues **you didn't create** — bug reports, incoming feature requests, anything that arrives raw. Tickets that `/to-tickets` produced are already agent-ready, so **don't triage them**.

- **Something's broken** → **`/diagnosing-bugs`**. For the hard ones: the bug that resists a first glance, the intermittent flake, the regression that crept in between two known-good states. It refuses to theorise until it has a **tight feedback loop** — one command that already goes red on *this* bug — then fixes with a regression test. Its post-mortem hands off to **`/improve-codebase-architecture`** when the real finding is that there's no good seam to lock the bug down.

- **A huge, foggy effort — a greenfield project or a huge feature build, too big for one session** → **`/wayfinder`**, the most cognitively demanding flow here. When the way from here to the destination isn't visible yet, it charts a **shared map** of **decision tickets** on the issue tracker and resolves them one at a time — producing **decisions, not deliverables** — until the fog is pushed back and the way is clear. Where **`/grill-with-docs`** sharpens an idea you can hold in one session, wayfinder is for the idea you can't — and it's slower and denser, so save it for exactly that, never a well-scoped feature.

  When the map clears, **it hands off, it doesn't build**: merge onto the main flow at **`/to-spec`**, which collapses the map's linked decisions into a buildable plan, then `/to-tickets` and `/implement` as usual. Looping the map straight into `/implement` skips that collapse and throws the linked detail away — go straight to `/implement` only when the effort turned out genuinely small.

## Codebase health

Not feature work — upkeep.

- **`/improve-codebase-architecture`** — run whenever you have a spare moment to keep the codebase good for agents to operate in. It surfaces **deepening opportunities**; picking one _generates an idea_ you can take into the main flow at `/grill-with-docs`. It's the survey that finds the candidates; **`/codebase-design`** (below) is the bench you design the chosen one on.

## Vocabulary underneath

Two model-invoked references that run *beneath* the other skills — each the single source of truth for its vocabulary. Reach for them directly when the **words**, not the process, are the problem; or let the skills above pull them in.

- **`/domain-modeling`** — sharpen the project's *domain* language: challenge a fuzzy term, resolve an overloaded word ("account" doing three jobs), record a hard-to-reverse decision as an ADR. It's the active discipline `/grill-with-docs` drives to keep `CONTEXT.md` a clean glossary.
- **`/codebase-design`** — the deep-module vocabulary (module, interface, depth, seam, adapter, leverage, locality) for designing a module's *shape*: a lot of behaviour behind a small interface at a clean seam. `/tdd` and `/improve-codebase-architecture` both speak it.

## Crossing sessions

- **`/handoff`** — when a thread is full or you need to branch off (e.g. into a `/prototype` session), this compacts the conversation into a markdown file. You don't continue in place — you **open a new session and reference that file** to carry the context across. It's the bridge between context windows, in either direction. Use it when you want a **fresh session** but need the **current conversation preserved**.
- **`/compact`** (built-in) — stay in the **same conversation**, letting the earlier turns be summarized. Use it at **intentional breaks between phases**, when you don't mind losing the verbatim history. Don't compact mid-phase — the agent can lose its way. `/handoff` forks; `/compact` continues.

## Standalone

Off the main flow entirely.

- **`/grill-me`** — the same relentless interview as `/grill-with-docs`, but for when you have **no codebase**. Stateless: it saves nothing locally, builds no `CONTEXT.md`. Reach for it to sharpen any plan or design that doesn't live in a repo.
- **`/prototype`** — a small, throwaway program that answers one design question: does this state model feel right, or what should this UI look like. Throwaway from day one — keep the answer, delete the code. It's the detour in step 2 of the main flow, but reach for it any time a design question is hard to settle on paper.
- **`/research`** — delegate reading legwork to a **background agent**: it investigates a question against **primary sources**, then leaves a cited Markdown file in the repo. Keep working while it reads. The file it produces is something to take *into* the main flow at `/grill-with-docs` — research feeds the thinking, it doesn't replace it.
- **`/teach`** — learn a concept over multiple sessions, using the current directory as a stateful workspace.
- **`/writing-great-skills`** — reference for writing and editing skills well.

## Precondition

**`/setup-matt-pocock-skills`** — run before your first engineering flow to configure the issue tracker, triage labels, and doc layout the other skills assume. Custom issue trackers also work.

### 2. Explore the codebase (optional)

If you have not already explored the codebase, do so to understand the current state of the code. Ticket titles and descriptions should use the project's domain glossary vocabulary, and respect ADRs in the area you're touching.

Look for opportunities to prefactor the code to make the implementation easier. "Make the change easy, then make the easy change."

### 3. Draft vertical slices

Break the work into **tracer bullet** tickets.

<vertical-slice-rules>

- Each slice cuts a narrow but COMPLETE path through every layer (schema, API, UI, tests) — vertical, NOT a horizontal slice of one layer
- A completed slice is demoable or verifiable on its own
- Each slice is sized to fit in a single fresh context window
- Any prefactoring should be done first

</vertical-slice-rules>

Give each ticket its **blocking edges** — the other tickets that must complete before it can start. A ticket with no blockers can start immediately.

**Wide refactors are the exception to vertical slicing.** A **wide refactor** is one mechanical change — rename a column, retype a shared symbol — whose **blast radius** fans across the whole codebase, so a single edit breaks thousands of call sites at once and no vertical slice can land green. Don't force it into a tracer bullet; sequence it as **expand–contract**. First expand: add the new form beside the old so nothing breaks. Then migrate the call sites over in batches sized by blast radius (per package, per directory), each batch its own ticket blocked by the expand, keeping CI green batch to batch because the old form still exists. Finally contract: delete the old form once no caller remains, in a ticket blocked by every migrate batch. When even the batches can't stay green alone, keep the sequence but let them share an integration branch that all block a final integrate-and-verify ticket — green is promised only there.

### 4. Quiz the user

Present the proposed breakdown as a numbered list. For each ticket, show:

- **Title**: short descriptive name
- **Blocked by**: which other tickets (if any) must complete first
- **What it delivers**: the end-to-end behaviour this ticket makes work

Ask the user:

- Does the granularity feel right? (too coarse / too fine)
- Are the blocking edges correct — does each ticket only depend on tickets that genuinely gate it?
- Should any tickets be merged or split further?

Iterate until the user approves the breakdown.

Work the **frontier**: any ticket whose blockers are all done. For a purely linear chain that means top to bottom.
